record.paper_title: Open problems in local discrete holomorphic dynamics
record.original_question: Associate computable invariants, ideally from a small class, to each holomorphic local dynamical system at the origin of C^n so that equality of invariants characterizes conjugacy as strongly as possible. In particular, can one construct complete invariant systems for holomorphic, smooth, C^k, or topological local conjugacy classes?

evidence.quote: (Q4) Find a way to associate a (possibly small) class of (possibly computable) objects, called invariants, to any holomorphic local dynamical system f ... The class of invariants is complete if two holomorphic local dynamical systems ... are ... locally conjugated if and only if they have the same invariants.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A holomorphic local dynamical system at the origin of $\mathbb{C}^n$ is a germ $f\colon (\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$ of a holomorphic map fixing the origin. Two such germs $f$ and $g$ are said to be locally conjugate (in a given regularity class) if there exists a germ of a homeomorphism (resp. $C^k$ diffeomorphism, smooth diffeomorphism, biholomorphism) $\varphi\colon(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$ such that $\varphi\circ f = g\circ\varphi$.

An invariant is a rule that assigns to each holomorphic local dynamical system at the origin of $\mathbb{C}^n$ an object (for example a number, formal power series, combinatorial datum, or geometric structure) in such a way that conjugate systems are assigned the same object. A class of invariants is called complete for a given conjugacy relation if two holomorphic local dynamical systems are conjugate (in the chosen regularity) if and only if all invariants in the class agree on them.

Problem. For each of the following equivalence relations on holomorphic local dynamical systems at the origin of $\mathbb{C}^n$ (with $n\ge 2$):

(a) holomorphic local conjugacy,
(b) smooth ($C^\infty$) local conjugacy,
(c) $C^k$ local conjugacy for a given $k\ge 1$,
(d) topological local conjugacy,

construct a class of invariants—as small and as effectively computable as possible—that is complete, i.e. fully characterizes the equivalence class of every holomorphic local dynamical system $f\colon(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a broad classification question in local discrete holomorphic dynamics. Complete systems of invariants are known only in very special situations (e.g. one-dimensional parabolic germs via Écalle-Voronin invariants, Siegel-type linearization results, formal normal forms in dimension one). In several variables a complete classification—holomorphic, smooth, $C^k$, or topological—remains open in general; the problem is widely cited as a guiding open question in surveys of local holomorphic dynamics.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in local discrete holomorphic dynamics (zbMATH entry)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems in local discrete holomorphic dynamics, including the construction of complete invariants for various regularities of local conjugacy.
status_evidence.claim: The classification problem via complete invariants is posed as open in surveys of local holomorphic dynamics.

status_evidence.title: Discrete holomorphic local dynamical systems (Abate, survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of local holomorphic dynamics emphasizing that, beyond special cases (one-variable parabolic germs, hyperbolic and Siegel linearization), no complete system of invariants for local conjugacy is known in several variables.
status_evidence.claim: No complete invariants for holomorphic/topological local conjugacy of germs in C^n are known in general.
